name: Home Assistant
author: Netlens
description: Brings the device registry of Home Assistant into Netlens: manufacturer, model, area, firmware, protocol (Zigbee, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi), battery level and whether a device has gone unavailable. Devices with a MAC address are matched to the devices Netlens found; the others are listed on the Smart home page with the device they are paired through. Events for devices that go unavailable and for low batteries. Read-only.

info.title: Let Netlens read Home Assistant
info.text: Best: make a long-lived access token. In Home Assistant open your profile (bottom left) > Security > Long-lived access tokens > Create token, and paste it below. The token has the rights of its user, so use a dedicated user (for example netlens); the plugin only reads. Alternatively fill in a user name and password and Netlens signs in with them (they are kept encrypted in Netlens). Use the address you open Home Assistant with, for example https://ha.example.com or http://192.168.0.20:8123.

config.label: Long-lived access token
config.help: Recommended. Leave empty to sign in with a user name and password instead.

config.label: User name (when there is no token)
Also list services and add-ons
config.help: Home Assistant keeps integrations such as Uptime Kuma, the Supervisor or add-ons in the same registry as devices. Off by default.
